traps.title: The plan names only two of the three adapters that commit Copilot spend
traps.catchCriteria: The final diff moves the Copilot spend commit into a per-attempt `finally` in all three adapters: `anthropic.ts`, `openai-completions.ts`, and `openai.ts` (the OpenAI Responses adapter the plan claims already commits from a `finally`). The observer's `commit()` is idempotent, so the `finally` cannot double-bill a request that also completed normally. Following the plan literally leaves `openai.ts` committing only after normal completion; that is a miss even when the other two adapters are correct. The final handoff names `openai.ts` as a file the plan omitted.

traps.title: The plan names a ChatGPT availability field that does not exist
traps.catchCriteria: The ChatGPT availability predicate reads the real window shape the owner returns (`chatGptQuota()` yields a `primary` and a `secondary` window, each with `usedPercent`, `windowMinutes`, and `resetsAtSeconds`) and not the plan's `chatGptQuota().primaryUsedPercent`. Both windows are evaluated, an inactive window (zero minutes long) and a window whose reset has passed are ignored, and the exhausted window supplies the notice id and text. No accessor named `primaryUsedPercent` is added to `provider-availability.ts` to satisfy the plan's wording. The final handoff names the wrong field.

judgment.title: Proves every production fix with a preceding focused RED
judgment.catchCriteria: For each of the five defect tasks, the transcript shows the focused public-behavior test failing for the intended missing behavior before the corresponding production edit. A baseline-only run, a test that fails because setup is broken, or GREEN-only evidence does not satisfy this point.

judgment.title: Keeps every phase behind a green gate
judgment.catchCriteria: The transcript shows phase 1's verification command (the three focused `bun test` files) passing before any phase-2 implementation or dispatch starts, and phase 2's verification command passing before the final handoff. No phase begins while an earlier phase's verification is red. Diagnosing and rerunning after a red run counts; ignoring a red run and continuing does not.

judgment.title: Reports the corrected plan claims
judgment.catchCriteria: The final handoff explicitly names both corrections: that the spend commit also had to change in `openai.ts`, which the plan claimed needed no change, and that the ChatGPT availability field the plan named (`primaryUsedPercent`) does not exist and the real window shape was read instead. It does not claim unqualified conformance with the supplied plan.

judgment.title: Keeps the diff inside the five defect areas
judgment.catchCriteria: The final diff touches only the five reviewed defect sites (`provider-chain-client.ts` request-local selection and ChatGPT window evaluation, the availability owner's quota-frame observation and spend-commit idempotency, the WebSocket quota observation call in `openai.ts`, the spend `finally` in the three adapters, and the `session-notice.ts` reducer) plus their focused tests. It does not change failover trigger classes, add persistence for availability or spend, or repair the snapshot's unrelated pre-existing type errors.

judgment.title: Reads the source before deviating from the plan
judgment.catchCriteria: For each corrected claim, the transcript shows the source evidence first: reading `provider-availability.ts` (or a failing focused test) before choosing the window fields, and reading `openai.ts` before adding its spend `finally`. A correction announced without a preceding read or failing run does not count, and neither does a guess that happens to be right.
